title: Every non-neat nonconstant periodic orbit of a smooth Hamiltonian with positive definite fiber Hessian is a round trip
source_title: Non-degeneracy of closed orbits for generic potentials
author: Patrick Bernard
difficulty_reason: Local uniqueness of Hamiltonian trajectories does not classify all returns of their projections to the base, and a non-neat orbit can contain both degenerate and self-intersection times. The author rules out transverse self-intersections globally, uses the energy-preserving fiber symmetry to construct a decreasing involution on every nondegenerate interval, and closes the time circle at the two turning points. The square-root coordinate then gives smoothness through the turning points, providing the new global round-trip classification beyond the ordinary local implicit-function theorem.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Proposition1 for a nonconstant periodic orbit of minimal periodT of a smooth Hamiltonian on a cotangent bundle whose fiber Hessian is positive definite. Non-neat means no nontrivial embedded base segment disjoint from the remaining projection. The conclusion is a smooth orientation-reversing time-circle diffeomorphism sigma preserving the base projection, with two fixed turning times at which its derivative is-1 and the base velocity vanishes. Read full new symmetry construction8–11 and all projected-orbit classification11–13 through its proof completion. The written smooth square-root construction supplies turning-point regularity; no generic nondegeneracy theorem or arbitrary Hamiltonian extension is claimed. Source Lemma6 labels the previously defined function as h rather than f, and11 has a duplicated typeset composite, while the defining equation and explicit conjugacy gSh immediately specify the construction; retain originals. PDF author Patrick Bernard and11/2024/255/license verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author uses the energy-preserving fiber symmetry and a global classification of projected self-intersections to construct an orientation-reversing involution of the periodic time circle, then resolves its turning points with a smooth square-root coordinate. This geometric classification supports the missing libration case in generic Hamiltonian nondegeneracy and exceeds qualifying-exam Hamiltonian theory.
